children: UBS drew a comparison to NFL team valuations when analyzing how investors might consider justifying the premium valuations of Costco
, which has smashed the return of the broad stock market over the last 20 years.

Analyst Michael Lasser highlighted that sports franchises are clear examples of how much value investors can assign to what he said were scarce, difficult-to-replicate assets with durable consumer relationships, recurring engagement, bargaining power, and multiple opportunities to monetize the same ecosystem.

The value of the average NFL team has increased more than 30% in just one year to close to $10B. The average valuation is estimated to be approximately 13.4X revenue and roughly a high-20s to low-30s multiple of EBITDA. The Dallas Cowboys are considered the most valuable NFL franchise, with an estimated value of $16B. The future looks bright for the league as TV viewership continues to soar, apparel sales are up double digits, and international expansion is leading to new markets.

The underlying NFL assets have some key characteristics to support lofty valuations, such as scarcity, durable brands, a deeply engaged customer base, significant bargaining power, and multiple ways to monetize the same group of fans. Sound familiar? Some Costco
bulls claim those same attributes exist.

professional sports franchise kinship includes approximately 145M cardholders, approximately 90% renewal rates, 914 warehouses, roughly $270B of annual sales, and $5.3B of membership fee revenue. "A Costco membership can be thought of much like a season ticket. The customer pays upfront to participate in the ecosystem. Costco then has repeated opportunities to monetize that relationship through merchandise," highlighted Lasser.

economic flywheel of membership, traffic, sales, supplier leverage, Kirkland, data, advertising, digital, and higher membership value could keep valuations churning higher as the NFL continues to see.
